text:
maya: Heads-up — prefetched/prompt cache hit-rate dropped sharply for model-owl-large on /summarize. Tenant=AcmeCorp, 6h token-saved down ~42%. Saw the dip right after yesterday's batching heuristic tweak. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/p/zkY3Y/prefetch-hit-overview :eyes:

samir: Can you paste the exact panel query? also which rollout did we deploy (canary -> stable)?

maya: panel query below (copied from panel):
```
sum by(customer, model, route) (increase(prefetch.cache_hits_total[6h])) / sum by(customer, model, route) (increase(prefetch.requests_total[6h]))
```
Filter: route="/summarize", model="model-owl-large"

june: fyi i rolled the batching tweak to stable at 2024-11-08T21:14Z (commit abcdef1). That change changed max_batch_size heuristics and also touched the request coalescing window.

perf-bot: :warning: Alert triggered: prefcache-hitrate drop for model-owl-large @ 2456789020. Affected customers: AcmeCorp (impact: token-saved -42%), BetaInc (-12%). See incident playbook: https://wiki.redwood/internal/prefetch-hitrate-runbook

samir: two hypotheses: 1) key normalization/regression — the new batching path may be trimming prefixes differently before hashing; 2) changed request ordering increased cold KV lookups due to smaller batching windows.

maya: i ran a quick sample of recent keys; noticed more variance in fingerprint length. example keys (sanitized):
```
"summarize::preface:client-123::v2"
"summarize::client-123::v2"
"summarize::preface:client-123::v2"
```
Seems like prefix-truncation occasionally drops the `preface` token.

june: that matches commit note — we added `prefix_trim` to reduce key length for huge prompts. probably a bug in the trim window.

samir: run this quick fingerprint diff job (bigquery):
```bash
bq query --nouse_legacy_sql '\nSELECT key_fp, COUNT(*) as cnt, customer
FROM `redwood-prod.prefetch_logs.6h`
WHERE model="model-owl-large" AND route="/summarize"
GROUP BY key_fp, customer ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 200'
```
Compare pre-abcdef1 and post-abcdef1 partitions. If same logical prompt splits to multiple key_fps, it's our bug.

maya: starting the bq job now. also can we snapshot a few node profiles when traffic hits cold keys? i want CPU + kernel selection counters. ops can you enable perf sampling for canary nodes? :pray:

ops: enabling profiler on canary group, will capture `lprof` traces for next 30m and pin stable to previous batching heuristics. rolling back canary to abcdeff (pre-batching-tweak) now. ETA 8m.

june: i'll prepare a quick patch to disable prefix_trim for the summarize route to test. we should also add a unit test that preserves `preface` tokens when trim is active.

samir: also check kernel-selection logs — if the kernel fallback happened more often that could increase latency and reduce effective batching. query: `select count(*) from runtime.kernels where model="model-owl-large" and kernel != recommended and ts > X`.

maya: BQ job returned — we have ~18k keys split across 3 fingerprints for the same logical prompt shape for AcmeCorp. attaching sample: https://storage.redwood/samples/2456789012/key-sample.csv

perf-bot: Note: autopruner will re-evaluate cache-hit smoothing after rollback, expect metrics normalization within 30-60m.

maya: action items: 1) ops pins rollback (in progress), 2) june will disable prefix_trim on summarize route (in test), 3) samir will run kernel-selection counts + perf traces, 4) i'll re-run hit-rate dashboard after 1h and post numbers.

ops: rollback complete, canary pinned to abcdeff. profiler data uploading now (link in ~10m).

june: pushed temp config to disable prefix_trim for route `/summarize` in canary. will monitor.

samir: starting kernel-selection query now. gave it a 30m window pre/post — will post on thread.

maya: thanks everyone. if hit-rate recovers after rollback + disable trim we schedule a proper fix and add regression test + dashboard alert (per-tenant split). :thumbsup:

samir: quick note — add a panel that shows "unique key_fp count per logical prompt" by tenant, that'll surface this earlier. low-cost metric.

maya: agreed. i'll open a small dashboard PR after metrics stabilize.
